variants.headline: Party divides in two
variants.sub: The colony has seen a party divide into two organisations.
variants.body:
A political party has split in two in {colony}. The division is an organisational fact, not a complete explanation of the differences behind it. In considering {target}, readers should distinguish the break itself from unreported motives, ideological labels or claims about the balance of parliamentary strength.

The responsibility of {target} should be considered without presuming the split's cause or its eventual consequences. This account records an organisational division and reserves judgment on particulars not supplied.

variants.headline: A political organisation breaks apart
variants.sub: A split has divided a political party in the colony.
variants.body:
Party unity has given way to division. A party has split in two, making political organisation itself the subject of the news. The assessment of {target} should address that break without treating either part as the natural owner of principles this report does not specify.

The responsibility of {target} should be considered without presuming the split's cause or its eventual consequences. This account records an organisational division and reserves judgment on particulars not supplied.

variants.headline: Unity gives way to a party split
variants.sub: A political party has split in two in {colony}.
variants.body:
A split has produced two parts where a party previously stood together. That is the development established in {colony}. Readers considering {target} should not be asked to accept an invented account of the dispute or an electoral forecast as part of the factual report.

The responsibility of {target} should be considered without presuming the split's cause or its eventual consequences. This account records an organisational division and reserves judgment on particulars not supplied.
